summary: Reviewed all 3 files: ObfuscationSettingsViewModel.cs (HasErrors property), SettingsView.axaml (error-banner row + Obfuscation tab bindings), and ObfuscationSettingsViewModelTests.cs (2 new tests).

HasErrors = Errors.Count > 0 is a minimal, correct computed property. The CollectionChanged subscription correctly propagates change notifications without MVVM toolkit source-generator involvement — the right pattern for a derived bool property over an ObservableCollection.

SettingsView.axaml 4-row grid (Auto,Auto,*,Auto) is correct. Error banner in Row 1 binds to SettingsViewModel.HasLoadError (correct DataContext). Obfuscation tab TextBlock and ListBox both bind to ObfuscationVm.HasErrors — no residual IsBusy binding.

Two unit tests cover both transitions (false on construction, true on Add, false after RemoveAt). Toggle() calling Errors.Clear() at the top is correctly covered by the CollectionChanged subscription.
No blocking issues. No Fix-Forward changes applied. One documentation-forward logged for future reference.

comments.note: HasErrors computed property uses the correct manual CollectionChanged + OnPropertyChanged(nameof(HasErrors)) pattern. Errors collection has no setter (init-only), so there is no risk of losing the subscription through reassignment. Correct and safe.

Toggle() calls Errors.Clear() at the top of every run — this correctly triggers CollectionChanged, which updates HasErrors to false at the start of each toggle pass. The notification chain is consistent.

[documentation-forward] The CollectionChanged + OnPropertyChanged(nameof(HasErrors)) pattern for raising change notifications on computed properties over ObservableCollection is not yet documented in the project manifest. Consider adding a brief note to constraints.md or api-surface.md so future contributors know this is the established idiom instead of reaching for [ObservableProperty].
